newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end lower as interest rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end lower as interest rates rise.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed lower in slow trade Tuesday as yields on Central Bank short-term papers rose more than 180 basis points at a weekly auction, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index fell 0.53 percent to 6,240.83 as 19 stocks fell, 10 rose and 10 closed flat.
Trading volume was thin with just 1.168 billion bolivars ($2.4 million) changing hands, the exchange said.
Brokers said the market had expected yields on Central Bank monetary stabilization, or TEM, bills to rise.

Yields on six-month TEM bills -- the benchmark from which wider interest rates are set -- rose 182 basis points to 18.71 percent at Tuesday's auction, taking the steam out of interest in equities, brokers said.
"The session was very slow due to lack of buyers. There is not much interest in the market right now," said Reinaldo Uribe of the Multinvest brokerage.
The composite .MRCP Merinvest index also closed lower slipping 0.55 percent to 96.06.

Among heavily traded stocks, Electricidad de Caracas fell 400 bolivars to 5200 bolivars, steel company Sivensa fell 3.00 bolivars to 142.00 bolivars and telephone company CANTV slipped 9.00 bolivars to 2,011.00 bolivars.
Stocks were seen continuing to slip in weak trade in coming sessions with trading interrupted by Thursday's Labor Day public holiday.
